Admit.
Heard on I.A. No. 10314 of 2023, which is first application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved by the appellant.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 13.5.2023 passed by Special Judge (POCSO Act) /
Second Additional Judge to the Court of First District and Additional Sessions Judge, Ashoknagar (M.P.) in Special Sessions Trial No. 143/2020, whereby appellant has been convicted and sentenced under Section 504 of IPC to undergo rigorous imprisonment of six months with fine of Rs.500/-,
under Section 366-A of IPC to undergo rigorous imprisonment of three years with fine of Rs.1000/-
and under Section 376 (1) of IPC read with Section 3/4 of POCSO Act to undergo rigorous imprisonment of ten years with tine of Rs.5000/-, with default stipulations.

entities.text:
Special Judge (POCSO Act) /
Second Additional Judge to the Court of First District and Additional Sessions Judge, Ashoknagar (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted the appellant without appreciating the material and evidence available on record.

As per prosecution story, rape was committed by the present appellant along with co-accused Khilaiya @ Khillu and Shivraj,
however, prosecutrix has not supported the case of the prosecution and turned hostile in respect to co-accused Khilaiya and Shivraj though DNA report matched with co-accused Khilaiya @ Khillu who has been acquitted and is negative in respect to present appellant.
It is further submitted that present appellant has already served almost years of incarceration.
This appeal is likely to take long time to conclude.
Hence, prayer is made to suspend the jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.
Counsel for the State vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.
Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without commenting on merits of the case, I.A. No. 10314 of 2023 is hereby allowed.

Subject to depositing of fine amount, if Amit Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182289983/
1 not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.
